newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian political party office firebombed.
newsitem.headline: Serbian political party office firebombed.

text.p: The offices of a ruling Serbian coalition party were petrol-bombed on Thursday evening, Belgrade police said on Friday.
Two rooms were destroyed in the explosion shortly before midnight but there were no injuries.
No one has yet been blamed or claimed responsibility for the attack at the Nova Demokratija (ND) offices.
The bombing coincides with opposition protests in Belgrade against Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic and his ruling Socialist party.
Opposition leaders say the authorities have committed widespread fraud by annulling votes which gave the opposition victories in 15 of the 18 biggest towns in Serbia at local elections last Sunday.
The ND (New Democracy), close to Milosevic, on Thursday broke ranks and denounced election rigging, calling for the will of the people to be respected.
ND spokesman Rebeka Srbinovic said no local "power wielder" had the right to annul the choice of voters and their freely-expressed will in the elections.
The ND is considered to be the most democracy-orientated partner in the ruling coalition also comprising the Socialists and the Yugoslav United Left (JUL).
